Using the standard abundance notation,

\[
[X/Y]=\log_{10}\left(\frac{n_X/n_Y)_\star}{(n_X/n_Y)_\odot}\right).
\]

For Star 1:

\[
[\mathrm{Si/H}]_1=[\mathrm{Si/Fe}]_1+[\mathrm{Fe/H}]_1
=0.3+0=0.3.
\]

Thus,

\[
\left(\frac{n_{\rm Si}}{n_{\rm H}}\right)_1
=10^{0.3}\left(\frac{n_{\rm Si}}{n_{\rm H}}\right)_\odot.
\]

For Star 2:

\[
[\mathrm{Mg/Si}]_2=[\mathrm{Mg/H}]_2-[\mathrm{Si/H}]_2.
\]

Therefore,

\[
0.3=0-[\mathrm{Si/H}]_2
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
[\mathrm{Si/H}]_2=-0.3.
\]

The silicon abundance ratio is consequently

\[
\frac{(n_{\rm Si}/n_{\rm H})_1}{(n_{\rm Si}/n_{\rm H})_2}
=\frac{10^{0.3}}{10^{-0.3}}
=10^{0.6}\approx 3.98\approx 3.9.
\]

Answer: D
